checks.reason: 皝自征遼東 names Liaodong as the target of the campaign Huang led in person, and the current idiomatic text drops it. 'Campaigned against Liaodong in person' restores it, and 克襄平 stays 'captured Xiangping'.
checks.after: Huang campaigned against Liaodong in person and captured Xiangping.

checks.reason: 居就 is read Jū-jiù (就 jiù), so 'Juqiu' is a misreading of the county name and 'Jujiu' is correct. 'Installed as magistrate of Jujiu' restores the office 令 that the current text drops. 以城降 becomes 'surrendered the town', and 縣宰 becomes 'county head', which keeps it distinct from 令. Zhang Heng of Xinchang is unchanged, and the two people are not merged.
checks.after: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed as magistrate of Jujiu, surrendered the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the county head and capitulated.

checks.reason: The only change is the misread place name, from Juqiu to Jujiu (居就, 就 jiù). Everything else is unchanged word for word, including the office 令 (Magistrate), Ren's appointment (所署), the surrender of the city and Zhang Heng seizing the county chief (縣宰).
checks.after: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Jujiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.

checks.reason: The sentence opens with 皝 as its subject, but the current literal text has no subject before 'sent'. The new text restores Huang. It renders 屢為邊患 as repeated trouble on the frontier and keeps 將軍 as a title, along with 稱籓于石季龍 (declaring vassalage to Shi Jilong) and 請師討遼 (asking for troops to attack Liao).
checks.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly caused trouble on the frontier, Huang sent General Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong and request troops to attack Liao.

checks.reason: The proposed 'am unwilling to kill you' treats 恨不 as if it simply meant 'unwilling', which the scope explicitly rules out. Without any mark it also translates the Tongjian variant in place of the extant 恨不殺汝, which is an emendation made silently in English. The amendment keeps the word-by-word rendering of the extant text, 'I regret not killing you'. It adds the documented critical reading in brackets, citing 晉書斠注's judgment and both witnesses, and changes no Chinese. The first clause takes the proposal's wording, 'a long time'.
checks.after: I have dwelt in your state a long time; I regret not killing you [the extant text 恨不殺汝 is probably corrupt (晉書斠注): the Tongjian reads 恨恨不欲殺汝, “with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you”; Yulan 744, quoting the 前燕錄, reads 誓不殺汝, “I swear not to kill you”].

checks.reason: The extant 恨不殺汝 cannot be read word by word as 'unwilling'. I accept this idiomatic text only as a deliberate, documented following of the critical reading supplied for s0168. 晉書斠注 (the annotated critical edition of the Jinshu) judges 恨不殺汝 a probable corruption of the Tongjian's 恨恨不欲殺汝 ('with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you'), and Yulan 744, quoting the 前燕錄, has 誓不殺汝 ('I swear not to kill you'). 'I am loath to kill you' follows the Tongjian reading and fits the context: Han offers his pursuers the archery test so they can withdraw. The current 'I should have killed you' contradicts that context. The amended literal field carries the documentation, and the Chinese is not changed.
checks.after: I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you.

checks.reason: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何 has three parts: he never expected his resolve to go unfulfilled, he dies with lingering regret, and 'it is fate, what can be done!'. The current 'That hope dies with me—such is fate' squeezes these together and drops the closing question. The new text restores all three and keeps the closing quotation mark.
checks.after: I never expected that this resolve would go unfulfilled; I die with lingering regret. It is fate. What can be done!”

checks.reason: The current text drops 屢 (repeated), 邊 (the borders), the title 將軍 and the specific request for troops (請師), and turns 稱籓 into the vaguer 'submit'. The new text restores all of these. 'To declare Huang's vassalage' correctly makes the vassalage Huang's, carried by the envoy Song Hui, and Shi Jilong is rendered Shi Hu, as in s0061 to s0071.
checks.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly troubled his borders, Huang sent General Song Hui to Shi Hu to declare Huang’s vassalage and request troops to attack Duan Liao.

checks.reason: 相持旬餘 means the two sides held each other off for more than ten days, not 'a fortnight's siege'. 左右 are his attendants, not specifically his officers, and 勸皝降 names Huang as the man they urged. The new text matches the literal field and leads correctly into Huang's reply in s0066.
checks.after: After the two sides held each other off for more than ten days, his attendants urged Huang to surrender.

checks.reason: This 至今 shows a consequence ('it went so far that') and is not 'just now'. s0232 traces the disaster that Su Jun and Zu Yue's rage brought on the state to the late (故) Yu Liang, so the memorial looks back on that crisis. 'And now … has suddenly passed away' wrongly makes the dowager's death a fresh event. 'Matters came to the point that' fits the argument. It is different from 至今楚灼 in s0231, which really means 'to this day'. 發憤 and 一旦升遐 (overcome with indignation, suddenly passed away) are kept. No date is inferred.
checks.after: Matters came to the point that the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, suddenly passed away.

checks.reason: 'It came to this:' is the consequential reading of 至今, which the argument in s0232 calls for. 'Until now' gives the wrong sense of time. The rest of the literal text is unchanged word for word, including 發憤 (gave vent to her indignation) and 一旦升遐 (in one morning ascended to distant heaven). The memorial's date and the s0233 chronology caution are left as they are.
checks.after: It came to this: the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.

checks.reason: 建威 is an office title (建威將軍, General Who Establishes Might), not part of a name, and the current text drops it. The new text restores it, along with 威名夙振 (long-established fame and prestige) and 終不保全 (it would in the end cost him his life). It covers every part of 陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼: the feigned madness, drinking without restraint, loose hair, and singing and shouting. 'Murong Han' is the same person as in the current text, so no identity is changed.
checks.after: After Duan Liao’s defeat, Murong Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. Believing that his long-established fame and prestige would ultimately endanger his life, he feigned madness, drinking without restraint, letting his hair hang loose, and singing and shouting.

checks.reason: Writing 'Jianwei Han' presents the office title 建威 as if it were part of his name, which is a definite defect. 'Han, General Who Establishes Might' fixes it. The new text keeps 初 (earlier), Duan Liao's defeat, the flight to Yuwen Gui, 威名夙振 (his long renown) and 終不保全 (he would not stay safe), plus the feigned madness, drinking, loose hair and singing and shouting.
checks.after: Earlier, when Duan Liao was defeated, Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. He thought that, because his fame and prestige had long been renowned, he would not ultimately be able to remain safe; so he feigned madness, drank without restraint, let his hair hang loose, and sang and shouted.

checks.reason: 陰使察翰 means Wang Che was sent secretly to observe Han, and the current 'to spy' drops both the secrecy and the person being observed. 撫膺 means stroking the chest, not 'clutching' it. 商人 is rendered as merchant, and 無言 (he said nothing) is kept. The new text also matches the literal field.
checks.after: Huang secretly sent the merchant Wang Che to observe Han; when Han saw Che he said nothing and only stroked his chest.

checks.reason: 封諸功臣百餘人 has no stated subject, and Emperor Cheng is the subject of s0090, so 'He enfeoffed' quietly picks a grantor. cautions: This is an editorial review of English wording only. It is not approval of any date, identity, chapter or publication.

s0168: The literal-field amendment records the documented variants in brackets without changing the Chinese. If the project would rather keep critical apparatus out of the literal field, an acceptable alternative is to keep the current literal text ('I regret not killing you') and put the same 晉書斠注 note in the apparatus. Either way, the idiomatic text 'I am loath to kill you' depends on that note being kept.

s0233: The consequential reading of 至今 is approved on the internal logic of the memorial only. It does not date the memorial, does not date the dowager's death, and does not lift the existing s0233 chronology caution.
s0091: The passive English deliberately leaves the grantor unnamed. The held extraction attribution of the grant is not cleared.

s0086 (not a target; left unfiled because the reading is uncertain): in 竊歸駿馬, 歸 may be Yuwen Gui's name ('stole Gui's fine horses'). Both English fields currently say only 'stole (fine) horses'. Worth a separate check, but it is not filed as a definite defect.
